lines.s: 台灣黑熊是台灣體型最大的陸地哺乳動物，胸前有一塊像月亮一樣的白色花紋。牠們主要生活在海拔一千到三千公尺的山區森林，以植物的果實、嫩葉為主要食物，偶爾也吃昆蟲和小動物。由於森林遭到開發，再加上過去的非法捕獵，台灣黑熊的數量曾經大幅減少，目前估計野外只剩下幾百隻，已被列為保育類動物。近年來，研究人員在山區架設了許多紅外線相機，持續記錄黑熊的活動。專家提醒，登山時如果遇到黑熊，千萬不要轉身就跑，應該保持冷靜，慢慢後退。

lines.en: The Formosan black bear is Taiwan's largest land mammal, with a white, moon-like mark on its chest. It lives mainly in mountain forests between one and three thousand metres, eating fruit and young leaves and sometimes insects and small animals. Because of forest development and past illegal hunting its numbers fell sharply; only a few hundred are thought to remain in the wild, and it is now a protected species. Researchers have set up many infrared cameras in the mountains to keep recording the bears. Experts warn that if you meet one while hiking, never turn and run: stay calm and back away slowly.

lines.s: 台灣的資源回收率在世界上名列前茅，但在三十多年前，台灣曾經被稱為「垃圾之島」。當時，垃圾處理場不夠用，不少地方垃圾堆積如山，引起民眾抗議。為了解決問題，政府從1990年代起推動垃圾分類和資源回收，並實施「垃圾不落地」政策，要求民眾在垃圾車來的時候親自把垃圾交給清潔隊。後來，台北市又推出了「垃圾費隨袋徵收」，民眾必須購買專用的垃圾袋，丟得越多，付得越多，可回收的東西則免費。這些政策大大減少了垃圾量，也讓資源回收成為台灣人的生活習慣。

lines.en: Taiwan's recycling rate is among the world's highest, yet over thirty years ago it was called "Garbage Island". Landfills couldn't cope, rubbish piled up like mountains in many places, and people protested. From the 1990s the government promoted sorting and recycling, and introduced the "rubbish never touches the ground" policy: people hand their rubbish to the cleaning crew in person when the truck comes. Later Taipei introduced charging for rubbish by the bag: you must buy special bags, so the more you throw away the more you pay, while recyclables are free. These policies greatly reduced rubbish and made recycling a daily habit in Taiwan.

lines.en: Ms Lin, you are a diving instructor. Why did you take up coral conservation?

lines.s: 我在墾丁潛水二十年了。最近十年，我親眼看到很多珊瑚變白、死亡，這叫做「珊瑚白化」，主要是海水溫度上升造成的。看著熟悉的海底一天天變得荒涼，我覺得不能再只是當一個旁觀者。
lines.zh: 我在墾丁潛水二十年了。最近十年，我親眼看到很多珊瑚變白、死亡，這叫做「珊瑚白化」，主要是海水溫度上升造成的。看著熟悉的海底一天天變得荒涼，我覺得不能再只是當一個旁觀者。
lines.en: I've dived at Kenting for twenty years. Over the last ten I've watched a lot of coral turn white and die — that's called "coral bleaching", caused mainly by rising sea temperatures. Seeing the seabed I knew grow barer day by day, I felt I couldn't just look on any more.

lines.zh: 您現在做了哪些事？
lines.en: What are you doing now?

lines.s: 我們和大學的研究團隊合作，在海底建立了「珊瑚苗圃」，先把健康的珊瑚切成小塊培養，等它們長大以後，再種回受損的珊瑚礁。三年來，我們已經種回了五千多株珊瑚。

lines.en: We work with a university research team. We've set up a "coral nursery" on the seabed: we cut healthy coral into small pieces and grow them, and when they're big enough we plant them back on damaged reefs. In three years we've replanted over five thousand corals.

lines.zh: 一般民眾能做些什麼？

lines.s: 其實很簡單。去海邊玩的時候，選擇對珊瑚友善的防曬乳，不要踩在珊瑚上，也不要帶走海裡的任何東西。最重要的是，從生活中減少碳排放，因為海水變熱，才是珊瑚最大的威脅。

玉山是台灣最高的山，主峰海拔三千九百五十二公尺，也是東北亞最高的山峰。在日本統治時期，因為它比日本的富士山還高，曾經被稱為「新高山」。玉山的名字，據說來自山頂冬天積雪時，遠遠看去像白玉一樣。
現在，登上玉山主峰是許多台灣人一生中想要完成的目標。不過，為了保護環境和登山者的安全，國家公園對入山人數有嚴格的限制，想登山的人必須先上網申請，再通過抽籤決定。由於名額有限，有些人申請了好幾次才抽中。
一般來說，登玉山需要兩天的時間。第一天從登山口出發，走大約八點五公里的山路，到達排雲山莊休息；第二天凌晨兩三點起床，摸黑登上主峰看日出，然後下山。登山專家提醒，玉山海拔很高，登山者可能出現頭痛、噁心等「高山症」的症狀，因此出發前一定要做好體能訓練，路上也要放慢腳步。

lines.en: Yushan is Taiwan's highest mountain: its main peak stands at 3,952 metres, the highest in north-east Asia. Under Japanese rule, because it was higher than Mount Fuji, it was called "Niitakayama" (New High Mountain). The name Yushan (Jade Mountain) is said to come from how its snowy summit looks like white jade from afar in winter. Today climbing the main peak is a lifetime goal for many Taiwanese. But to protect the environment and climbers' safety, the national park strictly limits numbers: you must apply online and places are decided by lottery, so some people apply several times before they win one. The climb usually takes two days. On the first you walk about 8.5 kilometres from the trailhead to the Paiyun Lodge to rest; on the second you get up at two or three in the morning, climb to the peak in the dark to see the sunrise, then come down. Experts warn that at such altitude climbers may get headaches, nausea and other symptoms of altitude sickness, so train before you go and take it slowly.

在台灣，政府正式承認的原住民族一共有十六族，人口約六十萬人，大約占全台灣人口的百分之二點五。其中人數最多的是阿美族，主要居住在花蓮和台東一帶。
每年七、八月，阿美族的各個部落都會舉行「豐年祭」，感謝祖先和神靈帶來豐收。豐年祭通常持續好幾天，族人會穿上傳統服裝，手拉著手圍成一個大圓圈，一邊唱歌，一邊跳舞。在過去，豐年祭也是部落裡年輕男子接受訓練、學習成為大人的重要場合。
近年來，豐年祭吸引了不少外地遊客前來參觀。有些族人認為，這是讓更多人了解原住民文化的好機會；但也有人擔心，祭典被當作觀光表演，會失去原本的意義。因此，許多部落開始規定，遊客參觀時必須遵守部落的禁忌，例如某些儀式不能拍照，也不能隨便進入跳舞的圓圈。

lines.en: Taiwan officially recognises sixteen Indigenous peoples, about six hundred thousand people or roughly 2.5 per cent of the population. The largest are the Amis, who live mainly around Hualien and Taitung. Every July and August each Amis village holds a harvest festival to thank the ancestors and spirits for a good harvest. It usually lasts several days: people wear traditional dress, join hands in a great circle, and sing and dance. In the past the festival was also an important occasion for young men to be trained and learn to become adults. In recent years it has drawn many visitors from elsewhere. Some see this as a good chance for more people to understand Indigenous culture; others worry that treated as a tourist show, the festival will lose its meaning. So many villages now require visitors to respect their taboos — certain rites may not be photographed, and you may not wander into the dancing circle.

說到台灣的農產品，很多人會想到茶葉和水果，卻很少人知道，台灣也種咖啡，而且已經有一百多年的歷史。早在十九世紀末，就有英國人把咖啡樹引進台灣。日本統治時期，咖啡曾經大量種植，後來因為戰爭和市場變化而逐漸沒落。
直到二十一世紀初，台灣咖啡才重新受到重視。嘉義的阿里山、台南的東山、雲林的古坑，都成了有名的咖啡產區。近年來，台灣的咖啡豆在國際比賽中多次獲獎，有些豆子一公斤的價格甚至高達上萬元。
台灣咖啡之所以價格高，一方面是因為產量少，另一方面是因為人工成本高。台灣的咖啡大多種在山坡上，採收全靠人工，一顆一顆地挑選成熟的果實。農民說，雖然辛苦，但看到自己種的咖啡得到國際肯定，一切都值得。

lines.en: When it comes to Taiwan's farm produce, people think of tea and fruit; few know Taiwan grows coffee too, and has for over a century. In the late nineteenth century the British brought coffee trees to Taiwan. Under Japanese rule coffee was planted widely, then declined with war and changing markets. Only in the early twenty-first century did Taiwanese coffee win attention again: Alishan in Chiayi, Dongshan in Tainan and Gukeng in Yunlin became well-known growing areas. In recent years Taiwanese beans have repeatedly won international awards, and some sell for over ten thousand dollars a kilo. Taiwanese coffee is expensive partly because output is small and partly because labour costs are high: most is grown on hillsides and picked entirely by hand, ripe cherries chosen one by one. Farmers say that hard as it is, seeing their coffee win international recognition makes it all worthwhile.

lines.en: Temple performance troupes — lion dances, the Eight Generals, 'electronic Third Prince' dancers — are common at temple fairs. Members were mostly temple devotees, but professional teams have emerged, some invited to perform abroad. Some troupes, though, have a rowdy, brawling image, and some parents don't want their children involved; others now work with schools to teach the troupes as traditional art and change public perceptions.

lines.en: The weather bureau reports Taiwan's average annual temperature over the past decade is about one degree higher than thirty years ago. It seems small but is enough to affect ecology and farming: lowland plants are appearing higher up the mountains, and crops needing cold to flower and fruit, such as plums and peaches, have lower yields. Experts urge cutting carbon emissions and also preparing agriculture early with heat-tolerant varieties.

lines.en: My grandmother ran a snack shop in Taichung for fifty years, and I helped there as a child. I studied accounting at university and worked at a bank, but always felt something was missing. At twenty-eight I quit and spent two years training as a chef in France.

lines.s: 您的料理有什麼特色？
lines.zh: 您的料理有什麼特色？

lines.s: 近年來，越來越多台灣人選擇以「綠葬」的方式處理親人的後事。所謂綠葬，是指不立墓碑、不建墳墓，而是把骨灰埋在樹下、撒在花園，或灑入大海。這種做法的興起，一方面是因為都市土地有限，傳統墓地越來越難找；另一方面，也反映了人們觀念的改變：許多人認為，回歸自然才是生命最好的結束。根據統計，選擇綠葬的比例已經從十年前的百分之二，上升到現在的百分之十五左右。不過，綠葬在推廣上仍面臨一些阻礙。部分長輩認為沒有墳墓就無法祭拜，擔心子孫將來無處追思。為此，有些縣市在綠葬區設置了紀念牆，讓家屬可以刻上親人的名字，也有線上追思平台，讓遠在外地的家人也能表達思念。

lines.en: More and more Taiwanese choose 'green burial' for relatives: no headstone or grave, but ashes buried under trees, scattered in gardens or at sea. It has spread partly because urban land is limited and traditional cemeteries are hard to find, and partly because attitudes have changed — many feel returning to nature is the best end to life. The share choosing it has risen from two per cent ten years ago to about fifteen per cent now. But obstacles remain: some elders feel that without a grave there's nowhere to worship and descendants will have nowhere to remember them. So some counties have memorial walls in green-burial areas where names can be carved, and there are online remembrance platforms for family far away.

lines.s: 各位同學，今天的講座主題是「睡眠與學習」。很多學生在考試前習慣熬夜讀書，以為這樣可以多記一點內容。但腦科學研究發現，睡眠其實是記憶形成的關鍵階段。白天學到的新資訊，會在我們熟睡的時候被大腦整理，從短期記憶轉換成長期記憶。如果睡眠不足，這個過程就會被打斷，就算讀了很多，考試時也想不起來。研究人員曾經做過一個實驗，讓兩組學生學習同樣的單字，一組正常睡覺，另一組整晚不睡，結果第二天的測驗中，有睡覺的那一組記住的單字多了將近四成。因此，與其熬夜讀書，不如提早開始準備，每天固定讀一點，並且保持七到八個小時的睡眠。另外，睡前一小時最好不要使用手機，因為螢幕的藍光會影響入睡。

lines.en: Students, today's talk is 'Sleep and Learning'. Many stay up late before exams thinking they'll remember more. But brain research shows sleep is a key stage in forming memories: new information learned by day is organised by the brain during deep sleep and moved from short- to long-term memory. Without enough sleep the process is interrupted, and however much you read, you can't recall it in the exam. In one experiment, two groups learned the same words; one slept normally, the other stayed up all night; the next day the sleepers remembered nearly forty per cent more words. So rather than staying up, start early, read a little every day, and keep seven to eight hours' sleep. Also avoid your phone in the hour before bed: blue light from the screen disrupts sleep.

lines.s: 今天想跟大家分享的是台灣的「社區營造」經驗。90年代以後，政府開始鼓勵居民自己發現社區的問題，並且共同找出解決的辦法，而不是凡事都等政府來做。以南投的桃米社區為例，這裡在1999年的大地震中受到嚴重破壞，許多房子倒塌，年輕人也紛紛離開。後來，在專家的協助下，居民發現社區裡有豐富的青蛙和蜻蜓，於是決定發展生態旅遊。他們接受培訓，成為生態解說員，並把舊房子改成民宿。十幾年下來，桃米從一個沒落的農村，變成了知名的「青蛙村」，每年吸引數十萬名遊客。這個例子說明，社區營造的關鍵不在於大筆的建設經費，而在於居民的參與和對家鄉的認同。

lines.en: Today I want to share Taiwan's experience of 'community building'. From the 1990s the government encouraged residents to identify their community's problems and find solutions together, rather than waiting for the government. Take Taomi in Nantou: badly damaged in the 1999 earthquake, with many houses collapsed and young people leaving. With experts' help, residents found the area rich in frogs and dragonflies and decided to develop eco-tourism; they trained as eco-interpreters and turned old houses into guesthouses. Over a decade or so Taomi went from a declining farming village to the well-known 'Frog Village', drawing hundreds of thousands of visitors a year. The example shows that community building depends not on big construction budgets but on residents' participation and identification with their home.

They offer very diverse services: besides selling goods you can pay bills, send parcels, print documents and even handle some government business. Scholars say they've become community 'life centres'. Others worry that over-reliance on them is causing traditional corner shops to disappear.

lines.en: The black-faced spoonbill is a winter migrant, flying each October from the north to the Qigu wetlands in Tainan and returning in March or April. In 2002 only a little over a thousand remained worldwide; after years of conservation there are now over six thousand, more than half wintering in Taiwan. The local government set up a reserve and restricts development near the wetlands so the rare bird has a safe habitat.

lines.s: 各位聽眾，今天的節目要談的是「無人機送貨」。過去送貨主要靠貨車和機車，但在山區和離島，交通不便，一份包裹可能要好幾天才能送到。近年來，台灣開始試驗用無人機運送物品，尤其是急需的藥品和醫療用品。在花蓮的一個山區部落，過去居民要拿藥，必須開車兩個小時到市區的醫院；現在醫院把藥品裝在無人機上，二十分鐘就能送達。不過，無人機送貨也面臨不少限制。首先，它能載的重量有限，目前大多只能載五公斤以下的物品。其次，天氣不好或風太大時，無人機無法起飛。此外，在人口密集的城市，無人機的飛行安全和隱私問題也引起討論。專家認為，無人機短期內不會取代傳統的送貨方式，但在偏遠地區，它可以成為很好的補充。

lines.en: Listeners, today's programme is about drone delivery. Deliveries have relied on lorries and scooters, but in mountains and on outlying islands transport is poor and a parcel may take days. Taiwan has begun trials of drone delivery, especially urgent medicines and medical supplies. In a mountain village in Hualien residents used to drive two hours to a city hospital for medicine; now the hospital loads it onto a drone and it arrives in twenty minutes. But there are limits: payloads are small — mostly under five kilos for now; drones can't fly in bad weather or strong wind; and in dense cities flight safety and privacy are debated. Experts think drones won't replace traditional delivery soon but can be a good supplement in remote areas.

lines.s: 今天的文化講座要介紹台灣的「布袋戲」。布袋戲是一種用手操作木偶的傳統戲劇，大約在十九世紀從福建傳入台灣。早期的布袋戲在廟口演出，戲台很小，只需要兩三個人就能表演，內容多半是歷史故事和民間傳說。到了二十世紀中期，布袋戲進入電視，出現了許多深受歡迎的角色，收視率一度高達百分之九十以上，甚至有人為了看布袋戲而不去上班。後來電視節目的種類越來越多，布袋戲的觀眾逐漸減少。不過，近年來有團隊結合電腦動畫和特效，把布袋戲拍成電影和網路影集，吸引了不少年輕觀眾，也走向國際市場。表演者表示，雖然形式改變了，但操偶的基本功仍然最重要，一個成熟的操偶師往往要練習十年以上。

lines.en: Today's cultural talk introduces Taiwanese glove puppetry, a traditional theatre of hand-operated puppets brought from Fujian in about the nineteenth century. Early shows were at temple squares on small stages needing just two or three performers, mostly history and folk legends. In the mid-twentieth century puppetry moved to television, creating hugely popular characters; ratings once topped ninety per cent, and some people even skipped work to watch. As TV offered more, audiences shrank. Recently teams have combined computer animation and effects to make films and web series, attracting young viewers and reaching international markets. Performers say that although the form has changed, basic puppeteering skill matters most; a mature puppeteer often trains for over ten years.

lines.s: 大家好，今天想談談「食物里程」這個概念。所謂食物里程，是指食物從產地到餐桌所經過的距離。距離越遠，運輸過程中消耗的能源和排放的二氧化碳就越多。舉例來說，一顆從國外空運來的蘋果，它的碳排放可能是本地蘋果的好幾倍。因此，有人提倡「在地消費」，也就是盡量購買當地、當季生產的食物。這麼做的好處不只是環保，當季的蔬果通常比較新鮮、營養，價格也比較實惠，同時還能支持在地農民。台灣近年出現了許多農夫市集，消費者可以直接向農民購買，了解食物是怎麼種出來的。不過，在地消費並不代表完全不吃進口食物。有些食物台灣無法生產，或是產量不足，適度進口仍然是必要的。重要的是，消費者在選購時能多一分思考，知道自己的選擇會對環境造成什麼影響。

lines.en: Hello everyone. Today let's talk about 'food miles' — the distance food travels from farm to table. The further it goes, the more energy is used and the more carbon dioxide emitted in transport: an apple air-freighted from abroad may have several times the emissions of a local one. So some advocate 'buying local' — mostly food produced locally and in season. Besides being greener, seasonal produce is usually fresher, more nutritious and cheaper, and it supports local farmers. Taiwan now has many farmers' markets where shoppers buy directly from growers and learn how food is grown. But buying local doesn't mean never eating imports: some foods Taiwan can't produce or doesn't produce enough of, so some imports remain necessary. What matters is giving a little more thought when shopping, knowing how your choices affect the environment.

lines.en: Hello, listeners. Today: Taiwan's "forest therapy" — relaxing and restoring body and mind by walking, breathing deeply and sitting quietly in forests. The idea began in Japan and is increasingly popular in Taiwan. Research shows trees release substances called phytoncides that help lower stress hormones and steady heart rate and blood pressure. In an experiment with office workers, anxiety fell by an average of thirty per cent after two days in a forest. More than ten forest recreation areas in Taiwan now offer professional therapy courses led by trained guides. Experts note, however, that forest therapy can't replace medical care; serious problems still need a doctor.

lines.s: 今天的講座要談的是「食物里程」。食物里程指的是食物從產地到餐桌所運送的距離。距離越長，運輸過程中消耗的燃料越多，排放的二氧化碳也越多。舉例來說，一顆從國外空運來台的蘋果，它的食物里程可能是本地水果的上百倍。因此，越來越多人提倡「在地消費」，也就是盡量購買附近生產的食材。這樣做的好處不只是減少碳排放，也能幫助本地的農民，並且吃到更新鮮、更符合季節的食物。在台灣，許多城市都有假日的農夫市集，消費者可以直接向農民購買蔬果，還能了解食物是怎麼種出來的。不過，也有人指出，食物里程並不是判斷環保與否的唯一標準，例如在溫室中種植的本地作物，耗費的能源可能比進口的還多。所以，選擇食物時，最好綜合考量季節、產地和生產方式。

lines.en: Today's talk is about "food miles" — the distance food travels from farm to table. The longer the distance, the more fuel used in transport and the more carbon dioxide emitted. An apple air-freighted to Taiwan may have a hundred times the food miles of local fruit. So more people advocate buying local, purchasing ingredients produced nearby. It cuts carbon emissions, supports local farmers and gives fresher, more seasonal food. Many Taiwanese cities hold weekend farmers' markets where shoppers buy directly from farmers and learn how food is grown. Some point out, though, that food miles aren't the only measure: local crops grown in greenhouses may use more energy than imports. So it's best to weigh season, origin and production method together.

lines.s: 大家好，今天想跟各位分享台灣的「鐵道文化保存」。台灣的鐵路已經有一百多年的歷史，沿線留下了許多老車站、舊隧道和蒸汽火車頭。過去，這些設施在停用以後，常常被拆除或荒廢。直到二十多年前，社會開始重視文化資產，鐵道保存才逐漸受到關注。以彰化的扇形車庫為例，它是台灣目前唯一還在使用的扇形車庫，可以同時停放十二輛火車頭，每年吸引數萬名鐵道迷前來參觀。另外，有些廢棄的鐵道被改造成自行車道，讓民眾可以一邊騎車，一邊欣賞沿途的風景。鐵道局也會在特定節日推出蒸汽火車的復駛活動，讓年輕一代體驗過去搭火車的感覺。專家認為，鐵道保存的意義，不只是留下舊的建築，更是保存一段屬於大家的共同記憶。

lines.en: Hello everyone. Today I'll talk about railway heritage in Taiwan. Taiwan's railways are over a century old, leaving many old stations, tunnels and steam locomotives along the lines. In the past these were often demolished or abandoned once out of use. Only about twenty years ago, as society began to value cultural heritage, did railway preservation gain attention. Take the Changhua roundhouse: Taiwan's only working fan-shaped roundhouse, it can hold twelve locomotives and draws tens of thousands of rail fans a year. Some disused lines have become cycle paths where people can ride and enjoy the scenery. The railway also runs steam trains again on certain holidays so young people can experience old-style travel. Experts say preservation isn't just about keeping old buildings but about keeping a shared memory that belongs to everyone.
